name: Stablecoin yield lending
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Lending Dollars to Leveraged Traders
caseLead: The investment case rests on the demand of traders and market makers to borrow dollar stablecoins, which they use as leverage and as collateral to buy digital assets, and for which they pay interest above money market rates. The premium persists because many traders cannot borrow dollars from banks against digital assets, and US policy on stablecoins and banking access keeps part of this demand outside regulated lenders.
caseRest: The main risk is losing deposits when a lending platform fails or when a stablecoin loses its peg, which can happen within days. Losses are rare but large, because the yield earned is small compared with the amount lost if a platform cannot return deposits. A stable return history therefore overstates the safety of the strategy, as the failures of Celsius and of lenders exposed to FTX showed in 2022.
figNote: The large figure on each card shows the Bitcoin price at the extreme of the episode: its low in a sell-off or its high in a rally, in US dollars, where k means thousands. Bitcoin prices indicate how much leveraged trading was taking place, because borrowers of stablecoins are mostly traders who use leverage to buy digital assets.

events.title: Bitcoin rally lifts stablecoin borrowing demand
events.text: Bitcoin reached a record high near $69,000 in November 2021, and traders borrowed stablecoins in large amounts to fund leveraged positions. The strategy gained because high borrowing demand lifted lending rates and borrowers repaid their loans at the pegged value.

events.title: Celsius freezes withdrawals after the Terra collapse
events.text: Celsius, a large lending platform, froze customer withdrawals on 12 June 2022 after the collapse of the Terra stablecoin, and Bitcoin fell to a low near $17,600. The strategy lost because funds deposited with the platform were locked and later subject to bankruptcy claims.

events.title: FTX bankruptcy spreads losses to lenders
events.text: FTX filed for bankruptcy on 11 November 2022, and Bitcoin fell to a low near $15,500 as lenders with exposure to the exchange halted withdrawals. The strategy lost because platforms that had lent to FTX or its affiliates could not return deposits in full.

events.title: Yen carry unwind tests lending platforms
events.text: A Bank of Japan rate rise and weak US jobs data pushed Bitcoin to a low near $49,000 on 5 August 2024 as leveraged positions were closed. The strategy gained because collateral covered the loans being liquidated, so lenders kept their deposits and earned interest.

events.title: US tariffs lower Bitcoin and trading activity
events.text: The US tariff announcement pushed Bitcoin to a low near $74,500 on 7 April 2025 as investors reduced risk across markets. Results were mixed because borrowing demand fell and lending rates declined, although collateral covered loans and no major platform failed.

events.title: US stablecoin law supports lending demand
events.text: The US GENIUS Act, signed in July 2025, set federal rules for stablecoin issuers as Bitcoin reached a high near $123,000. The strategy gained because clearer rules and rising trading activity supported demand for stablecoin borrowing.

instrument: USDC and USDT lent on regulated lenders and onchain lending protocols; variable rate; withdrawable on demand
rules: Deposits split across at least four platforms; no platform above 25%; only loans backed by excess collateral; only stablecoins with monthly reserve reports
costs: Estimated network fees and platform withdrawal fees deducted from interest

marketWatch: Rehyn monitors the lending rate on stablecoins against the Treasury bill yield, the share of loans backed by excess collateral and the discount of each stablecoin to its peg, because these show whether the premium covers the risk. Stablecoin legislation, regulatory action against exchanges and large moves in Bitcoin are the events that matter most. A fall in borrowing demand would reduce the lending rate, while a failure at a large platform would test the diversification of deposits.

favourable.heading: Rising demand for leverage
favourable.text: Rising demand for leverage favours the strategy because traders pay higher interest to borrow stablecoins when digital asset prices are rising. In the 2021 rally, stablecoin lending rates on large platforms rose well above money market rates.

favourable.heading: Loans backed by excess collateral
favourable.text: Loans that require excess collateral favour the strategy because the borrower's collateral can be sold to repay the lender if prices fall. In August 2024 large liquidations on onchain lending platforms were covered by collateral, so lenders were repaid in full.

favourable.heading: Clear regulation and reserve rules
favourable.text: Clear regulation favours the strategy because issuers hold audited reserves, which lowers the risk that a stablecoin loses its peg. After the GENIUS Act became law in July 2025, issuers in the United States faced reserve and disclosure requirements.

adverse.heading: Lending platform failure
adverse.text: Platform failures hurt the strategy because deposited funds can be frozen or lost when a lender cannot meet withdrawals. In June 2022 Celsius froze withdrawals, and in November 2022 lenders exposed to FTX did the same, leaving depositors with claims in bankruptcy.

adverse.heading: Stablecoin loses its peg
adverse.text: A loss of the peg hurts the strategy because the deposited stablecoin is worth less than the dollars lent. In March 2023 USDC traded as low as about 88 cents after Silicon Valley Bank, which held part of its reserves, failed.

adverse.heading: Falling borrowing demand
adverse.text: Weak trading hurts the strategy because fewer traders borrow stablecoins, which lowers lending rates towards zero. In 2023 lending rates on large platforms fell below Treasury bill yields as trading volumes declined.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's peak-to-trough drawdown during each event, using the default backtest parameters above and the actual loss on any platform deposits that were frozen or written down. Each event window runs from the last weekly high in the strategy's value to its low.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects moves in Bitcoin prices, lending rates and the probability of a platform failure, which are then applied to the strategy's current platform split.
